title: camcraft-cli --skill install: --force writes through a symbolic link, and parent links are followed

body:
Follow-up of the review of PR #4011 (`camcraft-cli --skill <folder|claude|copilot> install`, #3751). The PR is `merge-ready` and waits for the next cut. This issue applies to its code.

## What happens

`install()` in `crates/app/src/cli_skill.rs` (lines 168-181 on `issue/3751-cli-skill-install`, head `5f4316003`):

- With `--force`, line 179 calls `std::fs::write`. The call follows a symbolic link. It truncates and replaces the file that the link points to.
- Line 177 calls `std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)`. The call follows a symbolic link to a directory. The skill file is then written inside the directory that the link points to.
- Without `--force`, the check on line 170 is correct. It refuses a symbolic link, also a dangling one (`path.is_symlink()`).

## What is expected

The command writes only into the folder that the user named. It refuses a target that is a symbolic link, with or without `--force`. The message names the path and says that it is a link.

## Fix approach

Before the write, read `std::fs::symlink_metadata` for the target file and for each parent directory below the folder that the user named. Refuse if one of them is a symbolic link. Write nothing in that case.

## Pins (suite `cli` of `camcraft-app`)

- `skill_install_refuses_a_symlink_target_with_force`: the link's target file does not change, and the exit code is 1.
- `skill_install_refuses_a_symlinked_parent_directory`.
- The tests that make a symbolic link run on Unix only (`#[cfg(unix)]`), because Windows needs a privilege to make one.

## Notes

- The work stacks on #4011 if it starts before the cut ("Overlapping issues stack").
- Priority `P7`: a follow-up from a review. The user must give `--force` and must have a link at the target, so no data is lost without an explicit flag.
